**Proposed mechanism:** TP63 (HGNC:12105) —LEADS_TO→ Ankyloblepharon (HP:0000574); TP63 (HGNC:12105) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal defects (HP:0001053); TP63 (HGNC:12105) —LEADS_TO→ Cleft lip/palate (HP:0000218); ITGA6 (HGNC:6054) —BINDS→ Integrin alpha-6/beta-4 signaling pathway (R-HSA-1280145); ITGB4 (HGNC:6063) —BINDS→ Integrin alpha-6/beta-4 signaling pathway (R-HSA-1280145); ITGA6 (HGNC:6054) —LEADS_TO→ Junctional epidermolysis bullosa (HP:0007346); ITGA6 (HGNC:6054) —LEADS_TO→ Pyloric atresia (HP:0002087); Integrin alpha-6/beta-4 signaling pathway (R-HSA-1280145) —DISRUPTS→ Junctional epidermolysis bullosa (HP:0007346); Integrin alpha-6/beta-4 signaling pathway (R-HSA-1280145) —DISRUPTS→ Pyloric atresia (HP:0002087). Mutations in TP63 lead to ankyloblepharon, ectodermal defects, and cleft lip/palate. Mutations in ITGA6 disrupt the formation and signaling of the Integrin alpha-6/beta-4 complex, which is crucial for epidermal adhesion and development, leading to junctional epidermolysis bullosa and pyloric atresia. Both TP63 and ITGA6 pathways converge on critical developmental processes involving epithelial integrity and adhesion.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in ITGA6 in patients diagnosed with junctional epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia, or identification of distinct molecular pathways for each disease that do not intersect at the level of epithelial development or integrin signaling. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic variants in ITGA6 in gnomAD populations at a frequency > 0.01%.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ITGA6 in both conditions could lead to targeted therapies for junctional epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia that might also inform strategies for managing ectodermal defects in related syndromes. Furthermore, the role of TP63 in epithelial development highlights potential therapeutic targets for modulating cell adhesion and differentiation in both disease contexts.
